name: QServe: W4A8KV4 Quantization and System Co-design for Efficient LLM Serving
authors: Zhao, Lin, Zhang, Zhou, Gou, Chen, Zhang, Chen, Weng
problem: State-of-the-art INT4 PTQ methods only speed up low-batch edge inference; in large-batch cloud serving the dequantization overhead eats the entire gain (measured at 20-90%).
mechanism: Two halves. Algorithm (QoQ = W4A8KV4): progressive quantization - quantize weights progressively through intermediate bit widths so each step's dequantization is itself cheap, keeping dequant overhead inside the W4A8 GEMM instead of a separate pass; plus SmoothAttention, which smooths the 4-bit KV cache quantization error by shifting it out of the attention score computation. System: compute-aware weight REORDERING so each tile's dequant work is balanced against its GEMM work, and register-level parallelism to hide dequantization latency, dispatched on CUDA cores rather than SMs - the paper's core insight is that serving throughput is governed by low-throughput CUDA-core work, not SM throughput.
speedup_reported: Paper's own claim (abstract): existing INT4 methods suffer 20-90% runtime overhead from dequantizing weights or partial sums; QServe achieves 'measured speedup' with the QoQ W4A8KV4 algorithm. COMPRESSION RATIO: 4-bit weights, 8-bit activations, 4-bit KV cache. QUALITY COST: SmoothAttention is what buys back the KV4 accuracy, but no paired accuracy delta appears in the abstract, so the number to carry is the 20-90% overhead figure - which is a NEGATIVE result about the field and the most useful thing in this paper.
